# Sirach Chapter 44 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 44 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 44 opens the "Praise of the Ancestors" (chs. 44–50), the most celebrated section of the book. The famous opening line "Let us now praise famous men" (ainēsōmen dē andras endoxous) must be rendered with full weight — this is one of the most resonant sentences in all ancient literature.

**Key decisions:**
- v. 1: "Let us now praise famous men" — ALL THREE agents render this identically. SOPHIA retains it without alteration. The word "now" (dē) is emphatic and must be kept. The word "famous" (endoxous) = glorious, celebrated.
- v. 3: The catalog of types begins here. The verse structure is a list; SOPHIA preserves it as such without flattening into prose.
- v. 9: The poignant counter-list — those forgotten. The pathos is essential to preserve.
- v. 16: Enoch — "taken up" (metetethe) rather than "died"; SOPHIA uses "taken up" consistently.
- v. 17: Noah as "compensation/ransom" (antallagma) — theologically important. SOPHIA retains "ransom" (LOGOS) over "compensation" (EMET).
- v. 20: "established the covenant in his flesh" = circumcision; no gloss needed.
- v. 21: The triple promise to Abraham (multitudes/stars/land inheritance) must be preserved as three parallel clauses.

---

**44:1** Let us now praise famous men, and our ancestors in their generations.

**44:2** The Lord allotted to them great glory, his majesty from of old.

**44:3** There were those who ruled in their kingdoms, men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and proclaiming prophecies;

**44:4** leaders of the people in their deliberations, men of learning wise in their teaching;

**44:5** those who composed musical melodies and set forth verses in writing;

**44:6** wealthy men endowed with resources, living peaceably in their dwelling places —

**44:7** all these were honored in their own generations and were a glory in their days.

**44:8** Some of them have left behind a name, so that their praise may be recounted.

**44:9** And there are some who have no memorial, who have perished as though they had never existed; they became as though they had never been born, and so too their children after them.

**44:10** But these were men of mercy, whose righteous deeds have not been forgotten.

**44:11** With their descendants their good things will remain; their blessing passes to their children's children.

**44:12** Their descendants stand firm in the covenants, and their children for their sakes.

**44:13** Their seed will endure forever, and their glory will not be blotted out.

**44:14** Their bodies were buried in peace, but their name lives on from generation to generation.

**44:15** Peoples will declare their wisdom, and the congregation recounts their praise.

**44:16** Enoch pleased the Lord and was taken up; he was an example of repentance for all generations.

**44:17** Noah was found blameless and righteous; in the time of wrath he was a ransom; therefore a remnant remained for the earth when the flood came.

**44:18** Everlasting covenants were made with him, that all flesh should never again be blotted out by a flood.

**44:19** Abraham was the great father of a multitude of nations, and no one has been found like him in glory.

**44:20** He kept the law of the Most High and entered into covenant with him; he established the covenant in his flesh, and when he was tested he proved faithful.

**44:21** Therefore the Lord assured him with an oath that the nations would be blessed through his descendants; that he would multiply him like the dust of the earth, and raise his seed on high like the stars, and give them inheritance from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.

**44:22** Likewise to Isaac he confirmed the same assurance for the sake of Abraham his father; the blessing of all peoples, and the covenant, he allowed to rest on the head of Jacob.

**44:23** He acknowledged him with his blessings and gave him his inheritance; he apportioned his portions and distributed them among the twelve tribes.
